newsitem.title: CANADA: Wascana climbs after takeover bid rejection.
newsitem.headline: Wascana climbs after takeover bid rejection.

text.p: Shares of takeover target Wascana Energy Inc climbed in busy trade on Tuesday after the company's board urged shareholders to reject Talisman Energy Inc's C$1.7 billion bid.
In early action, Wascana gained 0.25 to 19.20 on volume of 1.8 million shares, as investor hopes of a rival offer appeared to be rekindled.
Talisman, meanwhile, eased 0.05 to trade at 44.20, placing the share-swap value of its offer at C$18.12 per Wascana share.
Talisman has offered C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each Wascana share. Its offer expires on March 24.

Regina, Saskatchewan-based producer Wascana said on Tuesday that its board unanimously rejected the offer after financial advisers RBC Dominion Securities Inc and Goldman Sachs & Co ruled it was inadequate.
It said the deal would give Wascana a value that was below that described to oil and gas assets in similar transactions.
Wascana said also that Talisman's offer was announced before the release of the target's 1996 financial results, which showed stronger-than-expected oil and gas reserve additions and production.

"Increased reserves and increased production mean improved revenues, improved cash flows and greater value for our shareholders going forward. The Talisman offer takes none of this into account," Wascana chairman Ted Hanlon said in a statement. "In the opinion of the board, Wascana shareholders would do themselves a great disservice if they accepted such a low offer."

Wascana chief executive Frank Proto repeated that his firm was attracting strong interest from potential rival bidders and added numerous companies had signed confidentiality agreements and were conducting due diligence.
